items.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
items.summary: This method identifies specific fine-tuning data that inadvertently degrades model safety, helping developers audit training sets that bypass standard content filters.
items.authors: Saket Reddy, Amro Abbas, Anshuman Suri et al.

items.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions
items.summary: PerceptRL improves multimodal model performance by using reinforcement learning to fix visual perception errors that standard caption-based training often overlooks.
items.authors: Tongkun Guan, Zhibo Yang, Mingkun Yang et al.

items.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.summary: This framework filters out noisy or irrelevant agent failures before prompt optimization, ensuring that self-improving agents only learn from high-quality, actionable feedback.
items.authors: Zack Yu, Nicholas Lee, Minjae Lee et al.

items.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.summary: Researchers tested whether LLMs can autonomously discover unknown physical laws in simulated environments, providing insights into their capacity for independent scientific reasoning.
items.authors: Zhen Yang, Wen Wang, Xander Xu et al.

items.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
items.summary: The researchers developed a faster way for LLM agents to detect software vulnerabilities in real-time by reducing the compute-heavy reasoning steps required for security analysis.
items.authors: Amine Lbath, Massih-Reza Amini

items.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: EvoRouter optimizes multi-agent system configurations by using distillation to balance performance and cost, helping practitioners deploy complex agent workflows more efficiently.
items.authors: Yitao Xiao, Xu Zhang, Ye Cheng et al.

items.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
items.summary: DecisionRAG replaces traditional embedding-based retrieval with a decision model that evaluates document relevance directly, improving accuracy by avoiding the limitations of lexical matching.
items.authors: Chao Wan, Paul Jünger, Beixi Du et al.

items.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
items.summary: This paper introduces techniques for adding new languages to speech-to-text models without losing performance on previously learned languages, solving the problem of catastrophic forgetting.
items.authors: Yuchen Zhang, Haralambos Mouratidis, Ravi Shekhar

items.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
items.summary: The authors developed a compact, high-performance Persian retrieval model that outperforms existing small-scale alternatives, providing a practical tool for building efficient search systems in the Persian language.
items.authors: Yalda Taheri, Mohammad Hassan Heydari, Armon Rasooli

items.title: J-Comm: Jacobian-Guided Latent Communication between LLM Agents
items.summary: This framework improves collaboration between AI agents by allowing them to share latent reasoning states through geometric consensus and Jacobian-based interfaces, enhancing multi-agent problem solving.
items.authors: Xiangwei Wang, Wei Wang, Sachith Seneviratne et al.

items.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary
items.summary: This study mathematically analyzes how embedding geometry and vocabulary size influence the learning performance of linear token predictors, offering insights into the fundamental generalization limits of language models.
items.authors: Dario Bocchi, Matteo Negri, Flavio Nicoletti et al.

items.title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation
items.summary: The researchers propose a distillation method that transfers predictive knowledge from sequential recommenders to semantic-ID generative models, improving recommendation accuracy by leveraging item-level distributional data.
items.authors: Yixuan Xu, Hailin Liu, Linxiang Peng et al.

items.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
items.summary: The authors propose a framework for deciding when to trust an AI's output or escalate to a human auditor, helping practitioners minimize errors in high-stakes automated decision systems.
items.authors: Isaac Gibbs, Elise L. Han, Ryan J. Tibshirani et al.

items.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
items.summary: This paper demonstrates a cost-sensitive approach to AI classification that decides when an LLM should abstain from answering to avoid expensive errors, improving real-world operational efficiency.
items.authors: Sachin Gupta

items.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
items.summary: The researchers show that n-gram embedding tables in language models can be compressed using lower bit-precision to significantly reduce memory requirements without sacrificing performance.
items.authors: Stephen Chung, Wenyu Du

items.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
items.summary: This study empirically investigates whether reinforcement learning training induces power-seeking behaviors in language models, providing crucial insights for developers concerned about long-term AI safety.
items.authors: Barış Alparslan, Sandy Tanwisuth, Caleb Petterson

items.title: From Classifier Heads to Encoder Prototypes: Personalized Federated Learning with Head-Derived Clustering
items.summary: This method improves personalized federated learning by grouping clients based on their classifier heads, allowing for more effective model sharing without needing complex extra training steps.
items.authors: Amirardalan Dehghanpour, Arian Noori, Ehsan Tanghatari et al.

items.title: The End of Consensus Research?
items.summary: Researchers used AI to discover a new consensus protocol that significantly reduces latency in distributed systems, challenging the traditional reliance on purely human-designed algorithms.
items.authors: Clément Burgelin, Rachid Guerraoui, Zicong Hong et al.

items.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
items.summary: Quant-Arena provides a new benchmark to evaluate how well LLMs can autonomously perform the full quantitative trading research cycle, from hypothesis generation to strategy testing.
items.authors: Houde Qian, Zheng Jiang, Wenyi Li et al.

items.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
items.summary: ASTEROID uses a student-teacher framework to teach agents how to perform in-context exploration, overcoming the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning and imitation learning in partially observable environments.
items.authors: Sriyash Poddar, Yanda Bao, Jacob Krantz et al.

items.title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
items.summary: This system enables warehouse robot fleets to share a memory of past events without overloading servers by only processing visual data when specifically requested.
items.authors: Jad Yammine, Malek Wahidi, Abrar Anwar et al.

items.title: Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: The authors identify that agent training fails not just because of student errors, but because teachers often provide poor guidance in unfamiliar states, requiring better teacher-student alignment.
items.authors: Shu Zhao, Tan Yu

items.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
items.summary: This work introduces techniques to manage LLM memory usage by optimizing how key-value caches are stored and updated, preventing performance degradation during long task sequences.
items.authors: Tianyu Fu, Ruoxi Wang, Zihan Min et al.

items.title: When Do LLMs Help with Feature Selection? A Systematic Empirical Study
items.summary: This study evaluates when using LLMs for feature selection outperforms traditional statistical methods, providing guidance on when semantic context actually adds value to tabular data tasks.
items.authors: Fateme Memar, Dongjie Wang, Arvin Agah

items.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
items.summary: This framework improves multimodal agents by integrating external tools and memory, helping them solve complex visual tasks that base models cannot handle through reasoning alone.
items.authors: Yu Zhou, Cheng-Fu Yang, Rui Sun et al.

items.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
items.summary: This method prevents catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon agents by dynamically switching between specialized LoRA adapters during task execution instead of using static model weights.
items.authors: Rui Shi, Xunjian Yin, Jiacheng Sang et al.

items.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
items.summary: This framework improves multi-robot navigation safety by allowing robots to share uncertainty estimates, enabling better coordination in unpredictable human-shared environments.
items.authors: Zehao Wang, Jianpeng Yao, Yuping Wang et al.

items.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
items.summary: This study establishes a systematic way to measure how well language models improve their physical manipulation skills through self-correction, identifying key bottlenecks in their learning process.
items.authors: Zekai Li, Jiayi Yu, Jinlu Zhang et al.

items.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
items.summary: The researchers demonstrate that fine-tuning LLMs for one behavior can unintentionally trigger unrelated, secondary behaviors, which is a critical risk factor for developers managing model safety and alignment.
items.authors: Dongyoon Hahm, Woogyeol Jin, Dennis Wei et al.

items.title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
items.summary: This paper provides a framework to evaluate the reliability of LLM agents when they act as proxies for human stakeholders in complex healthcare decision-making tasks.
items.authors: Marco Boresta, Tommaso Giovannelli, Sepehr Namirad et al.

items.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
items.summary: The authors introduce a new speculative decoding method that improves inference speed for agentic AI by eliminating the need for historical KV cache, which often slows down long-running tasks.
items.authors: Jiaming Xu, Hanzhen Wang, Tianlang Zhao et al.

items.title: Tool Recommendation for Multi-Step Agents: Finding Every Tool a Task Needs
items.summary: This system enables agents to access thousands of tools by using a gateway that dynamically recommends the right tools for a task, bypassing standard context window limitations.
items.authors: Sam Partee, River Stevens, Thierry Damiba et al.

items.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
items.summary: This framework improves 3D object placement by grounding AI agents in physical laws, helping developers create more realistic simulations and interactive digital environments.
items.authors: Weichen Lyu, Chong Xia, Mingyu Dong et al.

items.title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers
items.summary: This Bayesian approach helps data scientists dynamically select the best models in real-time streams while balancing prediction accuracy with fairness constraints.
items.authors: Saatvik Kher, Hyungrok Do, Judy Zhong et al.

items.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
items.summary: This method uses a hierarchical architecture to efficiently fine-tune robotic manipulation tasks with minimal human intervention, making real-world deployment more practical.
items.authors: Zhefei Gong, Hefeifei Jiang, Zehao Wang et al.

items.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
items.summary: This framework enables AI agents to master complex video games using synthetic experiences, reducing the reliance on massive sets of human gameplay demonstrations.
items.authors: Mingyu Ouyang, Yiran Wang, Siyuan Hu et al.

items.title: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs
items.summary: The authors show that using back-translation with monolingual data significantly improves machine translation performance in low-resource languages compared to relying solely on few-shot prompting or fine-tuning.
items.authors: Divyanshu Bathla, Parag Singla, Jitin Singla

items.title: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
items.summary: This paper introduces a method to improve agentic reinforcement learning by selectively injecting and evaluating relevant skills, reducing the computational cost and instability of traditional rollout-based credit assignment.
items.authors: Wenlin Zhong, Hao Wang, Kun Yuan et al.

items.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The authors propose a framework that improves how LLM agents learn by assigning credit more intelligently across multi-turn actions, avoiding the pitfalls of uniform reward distribution without needing extra critic models.
items.authors: Bowen Ding, Mingda Wan, Yuhan Chen et al.

items.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
items.summary: By grouping robotic actions into chunks, this method reduces the redundant reasoning overhead of LLMs in control loops, making robot task execution significantly more efficient.
items.authors: Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu et al.

items.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
items.summary: Researchers found that LLMs produce inconsistent results for the same query even at zero temperature, meaning data scientists must account for non-deterministic outputs in production pipelines.
items.authors: Oktie Hassanzadeh, Dharmashankar Subramanian

items.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
items.summary: This study analyzes how LLM attention heads adapt their roles based on specific task contexts, offering practitioners better insight into how model components influence final predictions.
items.authors: Sovesh Mohapatra, Dani S Bassett

items.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.summary: The authors introduce a tool retrieval framework that uses real-time execution feedback to prioritize reliable tools, helping developers build more stable AI agent workflows.
items.authors: Weiliang Chen, Song Liao

items.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
items.summary: This paper presents a red-teaming method to detect harmful outcomes in AI agents by systematically testing how different service interactions can lead to unintended consequences.
items.authors: Yeonsung Jung, Zhiyuan Wang, Zifan Wang et al.

items.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
items.summary: Researchers found that LLM agents effectively use experimental feedback to tune neural operators, outperforming traditional optimization methods for scientific modeling tasks.
items.authors: Julian Chan, Javier Mora Jimenez

items.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
items.summary: A new probe-based monitoring system can detect hidden deception in LLM agents with high accuracy, providing a scalable way to improve AI safety and oversight.
items.authors: Oskar J. Hollinsworth, Alex F. Spies, Tigist Diriba et al.

items.title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization
items.summary: This paper introduces a more stable 4-bit quantization method for AdamW optimizer states, helping data scientists reduce memory usage without sacrificing training convergence.
items.authors: Hanyang Li, Shao Tang, Daniel Thomas Braithwaite et al.

items.title: SpaceCast-Bench: Evaluating Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: The authors introduce a new benchmark to test if vision-language models can predict how scenes change after interventions, moving beyond simple static image description.
items.authors: Hongxing Li, Jinyue Su, Dingming Li et al.

items.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
items.summary: The authors introduce a framework that moves beyond simple document retrieval by enabling models to compute and synthesize evidence across multiple sources, improving performance on complex reasoning tasks.
items.authors: Yilun Hao, Krishna Sayana, Isabella Ye et al.

items.title: EngramEdit: Decoupled Knowledge Updates in LLMs through Conditional Memory
items.summary: This research explores updating factual knowledge in LLMs by isolating it into a separate memory layer, allowing for targeted updates without needing to retrain the entire model.
items.authors: Hongru Cai, Ran Wei, Wenjie Wang et al.

items.title: Document-Level Text Simplification in Estonian Using Large Language Models
items.summary: This study evaluates how well current LLMs handle document-level text simplification in Estonian, providing insights for applying language models to low-resource, morphologically complex languages.
items.authors: Meeri-Ly Muru, Eduard Barbu

items.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
items.summary: The researchers demonstrate that robotic world models follow predictable scaling laws, allowing practitioners to better estimate the compute and data needed to improve robot planning capabilities.
items.authors: Artem Zholus, Nicolas Beltran-Velez, Jianhao Yuan et al.

items.title: Towards In-Parameter Memory Augmentation for Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes updating model parameters to store external knowledge, providing a more efficient alternative to long-context prompting for LLMs that need to retain domain-specific information.
items.authors: Haoyu Huang, Zhongwei Xie, Jiaxin Bai et al.

items.title: MINDSET: Energy-based Schema Evolution for Long Conversational Agent Memory
items.summary: The authors introduce a memory management system for conversational agents that dynamically updates stored information to ensure context remains relevant as user needs evolve over time.
items.authors: Sujato Dutta, Sreekruthy Tummala, Shashank Vanga et al.

items.title: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively
items.summary: Sherpa is a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes LLM teaching strategies based on real-time student performance, moving beyond static pedagogical rules for personalized education.
items.authors: Weixian Xu, Yanzhe Zhang, Zora Zhiruo Wang et al.

items.title: Agent in a Bottle: Can LLM Agents Turn Their Capabilities Into Cheap, Scalable Artifacts?
items.summary: This research explores how LLM agents can autonomously distill their problem-solving skills into smaller, cheaper models to handle high-volume tasks without incurring high API costs.
items.authors: Ankit Sonthalia, Haritz Puerto, Alexander Rubinstein et al.

items.title: T-Search: An Open Agentic Retriever and Playground for Hard Multi-Step Search
items.summary: We present T-Search, an open-weight agentic retriever for hard multi-step search. Given a question and a search tool over a fixed corpus, it runs a bounded multi-round search and returns a ranked list
items.authors: Olga Tsymboi, Ramil Latypov, Aleksandr Medvedev et al.

items.title: Balancing Memory Pathways: Analyzing and Improving Memory Utilization in Hybrid LMs
items.summary: Recurrent-attention hybrid language models (LMs), which interleave attention and recurrent layers, are increasingly used to combine the efficiency of the recurrent layers with the strong performance o
items.authors: Hyunji Lee, Joykirat Singh, Zaid Khan et al.

items.title: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents
items.summary: In decentralized consumer-to-consumer (C2C) marketplaces, people list goods, negotiate with strangers, and rate one another, so trust rests on reputation. Large language model (LLM) agents now act for
items.authors: Ziyan Wang, Shuqing Shi, James Oldfield et al.

items.title: Reading the Mood: Emotion-Guided Book-to-Music Recommendation via CGANs and LLMs
items.summary: Background music that matches the mood of a text has been shown to make readers feel more immersed and improve their reading experience, motivating recommender systems that pair books with mood-matche
items.authors: Manousos Linardakis, Georgios Alexandridis
